items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: The man that inspired me to play jazz first of all was Coleman Hawkins.

ctx.x: I guess I’m thinking of when you first got there, or maybe in the 60s especially.

Fortunately for me I grew up in a small English town, and there was no prejudice. The first black person I saw was a soldier that my father took in during the war. I revered them because of my knowledge of Teddy Wilson and Lionel Hampton and Charlie Christian, Louis Armstrong. The man that inspired me to play jazz first of all was Coleman Hawkins. And to me they were gods basically. I didn’t know anything about prejudice. But there was a theory in New York at that time, in the 60s, that — I didn’t live there per…
Uncle Tom is a term, are you talking about prejudice against white jazz musicians?
